newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch to permit NAM to test for gas in Wadden Sea.
newsitem.headline: Dutch to permit NAM to test for gas in Wadden Sea.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Thursday will allow Nederlandse Aardolie Maatschappij (NAM) -- a 50/50 joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon -- to test drill for gas at five sites in the ecologically sensitive Wadden Sea.
NAM would still not be allowed to produce gas in the protected area of the Wadden Sea even if the test drilling proved successful, the ministry of economic affairs said in a statement.
The government reviewed its strict policy in 1994 on the Wadden Sea, an unspoilt region of shallow waters and mud flats off the northern Dutch coast.
"This partial review says that '....gas may be drilled for under stringent conditions, and only so long as this gas can be produced from outside the Wadden Sea'" the government statement said.

The government says it will listen to public and industry reaction to the proposals. Meetings are planned between April 17 and April 23 to air objections and written submissions will be accepted until May 5.
NAM applied for the concessions to drill in December 1995.
No one at NAM was available for comment.
